newsitem.title: JAPAN: Site of Japan nuclear reactor rejects subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Site of Japan nuclear reactor rejects subsidies.

text.p: Japan's Fukui prefecture will not accept new subsidies for housing a prototype nuclear reactor until the cause of last year's sodium leak accident is determined, a prefectural official said on Wednesday.
The Science and Technology Agency plans to introduce subsidies starting next year for hosting experimental nuclear reactors and facilities related to nuclear fuel recycling.

Fukui Prefecture, which is located on the Sea of Japan coast, is the site of the prototype fast-breeder nuclear reactor Monju, plus one experimental reactor as well as 13 of the country's 50 commercial reactors.
Operations at Monju have been halted since a sodium leak accident in December 1995.
Fukui Governor Yukio Kurita told a news conference in September that new subsidies should be discussed only after the investigation into the cause of the accident is completed.

The Monju accident undermined the public's confidence in the safety of nuclear power plants, and contributed to a majority "no" vote in the country's first-ever referendum last summer at Maki, Niigata prefecture, on the construction of a nuclear power plant.
